context: A tutor and two students plan a campus food-waste audit.

sub_blocks.word_limit: Choose A or B. Options are on the question paper only.

lines.text: Now turn to Section Three. You will hear a tutor and two students discussing a campus food-waste project.
Questions twenty-one to twenty-four. Complete the flowchart. Write no more than two words for each answer. First, you have some time to look at questions twenty-one to twenty-four.
Now listen and answer questions twenty-one to twenty-four.
Let's lock the audit sequence before you start collecting.
First we design the checklist — what counts as leftover rice, peelings, that sort of thing.
Then we run a pilot in one kitchen so we don't change the categories halfway.
After that we collect the bags from the halls at the same time each evening.
And finally we weigh the contents and log the figures on the shared sheet.
Questions twenty-five to twenty-seven. Complete the summary. Write one word only for each answer. First, you have some time to look at questions twenty-five to twenty-seven.
Now listen and answer questions twenty-five to twenty-seven.
What's slowing you down at the moment?
Recruitment, honestly. Kitchen staff are busy and keep postponing.
We thought about paying people, but the ethics form only allows a small voucher.
Yes — a five-pound voucher, not cash.
How are you sending the invitation?
We tried posters first — wait.
Oh — sorry, actually email. The posters got no replies.
Questions twenty-eight to thirty. Who will do each task? Choose A or B. The names are on your question paper only. First, you have some time to look at questions twenty-eight to thirty.
Now listen and answer questions twenty-eight to thirty.
Split the remaining jobs so you don't both write the same section.
I'll handle the data tables — I'm faster with the spreadsheet.
lines.note: Paper: A Maya; B Leo. Data tables = Leo.

lines.text: Then I'll write the literature review, since I've already read the council report.
And the oral presentation to the catering manager?
Maya should lead that — she's clearer in meetings.
That's fine — I'll present.
Good. Send me the checklist by Friday.
That is the end of Section Three. Now turn to Section Four.
